story.hook: My cousin ruined the surprise twice.
story.script:
I had been planning my sister's surprise birthday dinner for nearly a month, and the only rule was simple: nobody was supposed to tell her where we were going. I booked the restaurant, collected everyone's food preferences, ordered a cake, and even created a fake family group chat so she would think we were having dinner at home.

Two days before the dinner, my cousin messaged me privately and asked whether he could bring his new girlfriend. I said yes, but I reminded him that the restaurant was a surprise and asked him not to mention it around my sister. He replied with a thumbs-up and told me not to worry.

The next morning, my sister called and casually asked whether she should wear something nice on Saturday. I froze. She laughed and said our cousin had posted a selfie from the restaurant with the caption, "Testing the place before the big surprise." He had tagged the location, tagged his girlfriend, and somehow tagged my sister too.

I was annoyed, but my sister said she would pretend she had never seen it. We agreed to keep the rest of the family unaware because everyone had worked hard on the plan. I thought that was the end of the problem. I even changed the reservation note so the staff would not accidentally greet her with a birthday message at the door, and I warned everyone again that the location was still supposed to stay inside our small planning chat.

It was not.

On Saturday afternoon, my cousin sent a message to the main family chat saying traffic near the restaurant looked terrible and everyone should leave early. For several seconds, nobody replied. Then my aunt asked which restaurant he meant. My cousin deleted the message, but by then the notification had appeared on everyone's phones.

He tried to recover by saying he was talking about a different dinner. My sister immediately replied, "Yes, definitely a completely different surprise dinner at a completely different restaurant."

The chat exploded.

My mother sent six laughing emojis. My uncle asked whether we should still yell surprise. My cousin blamed autocorrect, which made no sense at all. His girlfriend finally replied, "I told you not to send that here."

At that point, the surprise was completely ruined, so I changed the plan. I told everyone to arrive fifteen minutes later than originally planned, while I took my sister to the restaurant early. We sat at the table pretending we were waiting for a quiet dinner.

Then the whole family walked in together, holding the cake and singing badly on purpose.

My sister genuinely jumped because she had expected them to be waiting inside already. The restaurant staff joined in, my cousin arrived carrying flowers and looking extremely embarrassed, and somehow the failed surprise became funnier than the original plan.

Later, when we took the family photo, my sister made our cousin stand in the front holding a handwritten sign that said, "I can keep a secret."

He posted that photo himself.

For once, he remembered not to tag anyone.

publish.title: He Ruined The Surprise Twice
publish.description: He leaked the birthday surprise twice, so we changed the plan. #shorts #family #storytime
